items.title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
items.abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. A rear handle converts the diver’s grip into thrust and springs back to neutral on release; a diver-facing display shows depth, distance, battery state, and warnings. Six vector thrusters, with mounting angles optimized by gradient descent against drag-model thrust-ratio targets, are driven by an operational-space time-delay controller (TDC-OSF) that keeps the robot in the diver’s view; stereo vision and imaging sonar are fused for diver detection. In test-bed, tank, and sea trials, surge and heave thrusts matched design targets within 5–7%; approval-gated guidance held the robot 1–2 m from the diver with position and heading errors below 0.15 m and 3.5°; and the robot towed a diver at about 1 m/s and rose from 5 m to the surface in about 4 s. An underwater robot can thus serve as a physical safety layer for divers.

items.title: Designing AI-Driven Capability Ecosystems for Transforming Learning Beyond Traditional Training
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping how organizations build the capabilities on which their performance and resilience depend, exposing the limits of traditional training models that are static, episodic, and uniform. This chapter argues that meeting the capability demands of AI-augmented work requires a shift from training, understood as discrete instructional events, to continuous, embedded, and data-driven capability development organized as an ecosystem. Drawing on organizational learning theory, the dynamic capabilities perspective, sociotechnical systems thinking, and recent peer-reviewed research on AI in learning, the chapter reconceptualizes organizational learning for AI contexts and proposes a Capability Ecosystem Design Framework integrating technology, people, and processes. It examines how AI enables personalized learning pathways, embedded workflow learning, data-driven feedback loops, and the integration of formal, informal, and experiential learning, while taking seriously the risks of data dependency, algorithmic bias, and the over-automation of learning.

items.title: Designing Lunar Habitats for Long-Term Human Exploration: Insights From a Product Design Perspective
items.abstract: Deep space exploration research seeks to support long-term human presence on the Moon through innovative habitat solutions. Research on lunar habitats emphasises the need for integrated socio-technical solutions addressing extreme environmental conditions and human factors challenges through interdisciplinary design approaches. However, existing research mainly focuses on architectural and engineering perspectives, while product design frameworks for space product innovation remain fragmented. This paper investigates how product design approaches, methods, and tools can contribute to the development of habitable space infrastructures through a Research through Design strategy. The paper focuses on the integrated application of the Double-Diamond Design Thinking Model, Human-Centred Design and Human Systems Integration research phases and tasks to address the Space It Up! project research challenges on designing habitation means, crew stations, and logistics modules. The proposed framework is demonstrated through the development of the space-exploration habitat system strategic brief and the Moon Mobile Habitation concept, highlighting how the integrated framework, modelling and codesign approaches, and interdisciplinary collaboration translate human, operational, and system requirements into product design scenarios. The paper contributes a scalable methodological framework that systematises design phases, tasks, methods, and tools to support interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation for human-centred, mission-driven, and system-oriented space infrastructures.

items.title: Designing the Future of User Feedback for Generative AI
items.abstract: Post-deployment feedback from users can be a cost-effective, scalable, and representative means to monitor and improve generative AI systems and features. When implemented effectively, giving such feedback can increase users' engagement with and trust in GenAI systems. Government regulations and industry guidelines call for post-deployment user engagement, but there is little guidance on designing mechanisms that are usable for consumers and provide actionable input for product teams. We conducted a multi-phase study as a collaboration between academic researchers and eBay. Our benchmark evaluation of current industry approaches identified common issues including lack of discoverability, unclear terminology, and inattention to user value. Based on these findings, we developed best-practice recommendations and designed and tested a prototype feedback-collection tool. The tool aimed to provide users with an efficient, flexible, and positive feedback-giving experience, and provide product teams with rich data on performance and potential problems in a usable format.

items.title: Developing a Socratic Artificial Intelligence Tutor Using Retrieval Augmented Generation and Pedagogical Prompting
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as ChatGPT present a distinct challenge for computer science (CS) students. While they offer individualized learning support, unregulated use risks facilitating academic shortcuts and eroding critical thinking skills. This article introduces Lion-AI, a chatbot tutor developed to augment the CS educational experience. Lion-AI integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), rooted in university-specific course materials, with an engineered Socratic interaction policy. Unlike general-use tools, Lion-AI is designed to classify student requests, redirect direct-solution requests through diagnostic questioning, and provide guidance through one-question-at a-time interaction. The study describes a method for creating ethically constrained AI tutors in CS education. It presents the system’s three-tier architecture, the RAG pipeline, and the transparent interaction policy behind the tutor, positioning Lion-AI as a deployable proof of concept for combining curriculum grounding with explicit Socratic constraints. A controlled classroom study is planned as the next step.

items.title: Development and Validation of Human-AI Collaborative Workflow in SNOMED CT Mapping of Bilingual Clinical Text
items.abstract: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine-Clinical Terminology (SNOMED CT) is the principal international standard for semantic interoperability of clinical information, but mapping free-text clinical narratives to SNOMED CT concepts remains labor-intensive. We developed a large language model agent system for mapping bilingual clinical text to SNOMED CT concepts and evaluated its effect on mapping accuracy and efficiency within a human-AI collaborative workflow. We designed a three-module agent system comprising translation, abbreviation expansion, and vector-based retrieval components, integrated with a pre-embedded SNOMED CT vector database. Three health information managers independently mapped bilingual clinical text segments using three approaches: human-only, Agent-only, and Agent-assisted human mapping. Performance was evaluated by using hit rate, precision, recall, and F1 score at k = 1 and 5, and R-precision. Mapping time was compared between human-only and human-AI collaborative approaches. A total of 2,261 de-identified clinical text segments across nine clinical categories were collected at a tertiary academic hospital in South Korea. The human-AI collaborative workflow, which expanded the set of valid SNOMED CT candidates presented at each mapping decision, raised pooled hit rate@1 from 0.837 to 0.868 (difference 0.031, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.021 to 0.042; p < 0.001), raised R-precision from 0.632 to 0.674 (difference 0.042, 95% CI 0.034 to 0.051; p < 0.001), and reduced total mapping time by 53.9% (from 1.57 to 0.72 min per segment, including agent processing). By expanding the space of valid SNOMED CT candidates available to expert mappers, the human-AI collaborative approach improved SNOMED CT mapping accuracy while reducing time by about half. Its modular architecture, supporting periodic vector database updates without retraining, offers a sustainable and efficient solution for bilingual clinical terminology standardization.

items.title: Differences in prevalence and predictive value of metabolic syndrome
items.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is common in Chinese adults, but evidence regarding its burden and cardiovascular relevance among young healthcare workers (HCWs) remains limited. Different MetS definitions can yield materially different prevalence estimates and risk classifications. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 420 HCWs aged 20 to 45 years who underwent mandatory annual health examinations at a tertiary hospital in China from 2022 to 2024. Demographic, occupational, anthropometric, and biochemical data were extracted from health examination and personnel records. MetS was defined using the International Diabetes Federation (IDF), revised National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP ATP III), and Chinese Diabetes Society (CDS) criteria. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk was estimated using the China-PAR equations, with elevated estimated risk defined as ≥10%. items.title: Digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability: Basis for a maritime technology adoption framework for Filipino seafarers
items.abstract: This study assessed the digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability of Filipino seafarers and proposed a Maritime Technology Adoption Framework.The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, and 384 Filipino seafarers were selected using purposive sampling.Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire adapted from the DigComp Framework, contemporary maritime artificial intelligence utilization models, and innovation capability frameworks.The results revealed that Filipino seafarers demonstrated a high level of digital competence (CM = 3.55), with Information Literacy obtaining the highest assessment.Likewise, respondents exhibited a high extent of artificial intelligence utilization (CM = 3.79), with the Human Element dimension receiving the highest rating, highlighting the continued importance of human judgment in AIassisted operations.Furthermore, Filipino seafarers showed a high level of innovation capability (CM = 3.68), with Performance emerging as the highest-rated dimension.Correlation analysis indicated significant relationships between selected dimensions of digital competence and artificial intelligence utilization, as well as between selected dimensions of artificial intelligence utilization and innovation capability.However, no significant relationship was found between digital competence and innovation capability.A framework for Maritime Technology Adoption for Filipino Seafarers was developed based on the findings of the study.The framework identifies Digital Competence as the foundation, Artificial Intelligence Utilization as the enabling mechanism, and Innovation Capability as the outcome, highlighting both the direct and indirect pathways through which digital competence strengthens innovation capability.The framework provides a structured guide for workforce readiness and maritime digital transformation.

items.title: Digital Transformation in Commerce & Business Management: Emerging Trends and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a fundamental driver of change in commerce and business management, reshaping how organisations operate, compete, and create value. The integration of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain, Internet of Things, automation, and digital payment systems has transformed traditional business models and consumer interactions. This paper examines the emerging trends in digital transformation and evaluates their implications for commerce and business management. It focuses on the increasing adoption of e-commerce, data-driven decision-making, intelligent automation, personalised customer experiences, digital supply chains, and platform-based business models. The study also considers challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, digital skills, technological costs, and organisational resistance to change. Further, it explores future prospects associated with artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, immersive technologies, and sustainable digital business practices. The paper highlights the need for organisations to develop adaptive strategies, technological capabilities, and digitally skilled human resources to achieve sustainable growth in an increasingly technology-driven business environment

items.title: Digital Trust under Autonomous AI and Quantum Risk: Signed Memory, Cryptographic Unpredictability, and Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later
items.abstract: Governments are adopting artificial intelligence at the same moment that the cryptographic assumptions under their long-lived secrets are being placed on a clock. This paper treats four developments as a single problem of digital trust rather than as separate technical topics. First, AI systems are moving from content generation to agentic action, and are already exposed to impersonation, poisoning and unauthorised use. Second, persistent memory across sessions creates a new class of institutional record, whose integrity cannot be reduced to a signature. Third, cryptographic security depends on unpredictable keys, not on non-determinism, and better randomness does not answer a quantum attack on public-key mathematics. Fourth, harvest-now-decrypt-later means that the threat to data which must remain confidential for decades exists before a cryptographically relevant quantum computer does. Drawing on published resource estimates, the NIST post-quantum standards, and the positions of major security agencies on quantum key distribution, the paper argues that preparation should begin with an inventory of vulnerable cryptography, hybrid migration of high-value key exchange, and an explicit regime for the ownership and correction of AI memory. The implications for diplomatic communications and for states with constrained compute and language resources are developed throughout. items.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
items.abstract: Distillation has become a core primitive of large language model training, but its properties are not yet well understood. We take an entropic perspective, studying how the entropy of the student depends on the data and the divergence that define the distillation objective. We prove that forward KL inflates the entropy of the student above that of the teacher. Since cross-entropy training is a special case, this yields an identity that we verify quantitatively in pretraining and supervised finetuning. Other divergences come with no such guarantee: reverse KL deflates entropy until the gap between student and teacher gets too large, and interpolating between the two changes entropy smoothly early in training but abruptly at convergence. The lower entropy of on-policy distillation comes from token-level reverse KL, not from on-policy sampling. The divergence therefore acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, whose role is clearest in self-distillation: as conditioning on privileged information deflates entropy, the divergence hyperparameters that work best are those that compensate for it.

items.title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs
items.abstract: Ensuring the safe and reliable deployment of large language models (LLMs) remains a fundamental challenge. Existing safety alignment approaches either incur high computational cost or unintentionally disrupt the model's core knowledge, leading to degraded fluency and factual accuracy on benign tasks. This reveals a persistent trade-off between safety and utility. We propose DNAlign, a lightweight alignment framework that integrates control-theoretic optimization with null-space projection. By treating the LLM as a dynamic system, the proposed framework introduces controllable perturbations to steer generation toward safe behavior. A key component is the projection module, which restricts these perturbations to the harmful-related subspace derived from neutral hidden states, thereby preserving general knowledge and response quality. A value function trained on human preference data adaptively optimizes the control signals to align with human safety preferences. Extensive evaluations across multiple LLM backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently reduces harmful outputs while maintaining fluency, coherence, and factual utility. It achieves superior overall performance compared to prior alignment baselines without sacrificing generation diversity. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and practically deployable solution for safe LLM alignment. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DNAlign.

items.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support legal practice, education, and research, yet their reliability in national legal systems outside the United States remains largely undocumented. We introduce an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating LLM reliability on the Colombian legal system. The benchmark comprises 1,042 items spanning ten areas of law and three question formats (closed multiple-choice, semi-open, and open-ended IRAC), built through a human-in-the-loop pipeline with multi-stage expert review. We evaluate 15 contemporary proprietary and open-weight models with format-appropriate metrics. Accuracy on closed questions ranges widely, from 0.905 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) to 0.577, but on free-text legal answers factual correctness never exceeds 0.45 (on a 0-1 scale) for any model. We find a dissociation between answer relevancy and correctness (Spearman rho = -0.46): models reliably sound responsive while frequently being wrong, a pattern of particular concern for non-expert users. Closed-question accuracy and free-text correctness are strongly rank-correlated (rho = 0.94), so cheap multiple-choice screening predicts model ranking but overstates absolute reliability. An independent rubric-based LLM judge and blind human expert scoring both reproduce the free-text ranking (rho >= 0.88). The judge further reveals that only about half of the norms models cite are correct; the rest are wrong or non-existent. Reliability varies systematically by legal area and follows an inverted-U across question complexity. Our results indicate that current LLMs require expert supervision for Colombian legal tasks, and that grounding answers in authoritative sources is a promising path to higher reliability. We release the benchmark construction pipeline to support reproducible evaluation.

items.title: Does Shared Reading Promote Cognitive Development? A Literature Review
items.abstract: Shared reading is recognized as an educational method that promotes language development and emergent literacy during early childhood. However, growing evidence suggests that it influences additional developmental domains. This review examined empirical and theoretical literature with the aim of uncovering the potential of shared reading as an inclusive pedagogical approach for supporting children’s cognitive development by integrating findings on adult mediation, dialogic interaction, repeated reading, mental state discourse, instructional adaptations, and shared reading across diverse learner populations. The reviewed literature indicates that the effectiveness of shared reading depends primarily on the quality of the adult–child interaction. Adult mediation, instructional scaffolding, collaborative dialogue, and active child participation were found to be key instruments for supporting learning across home, preschool, and inclusive educational settings. Studies involving children with developmental disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, deafness, and deafblindness indicate that adapted shared reading promotes participation and advances language, communication, and broader developmental outcomes. Significant conceptual, methodological, and population-related gaps were found. Furthermore, few studies examined the contribution of shared reading to higher-order cognitive processes, such as executive functions, metacognition, inferential reasoning, cognitive flexibility, and critical thinking. Research on culturally and linguistically diverse populations, particularly Arabic-speaking learners, is also limited. This review proposes a reconceptualization of shared reading as an inclusive cognitive pedagogy in which adult mediation, dialogic interaction, instructional scaffolding, and collaborative meaning-making together promote children’s cognitive engagement and higher-order thinking.

items.title: DyadMem: A Long-Term Memory Benchmark of How Agents Work with Users
items.abstract: Long-term agents must remember not only what is true about a user, but also how a particular agent should work with that user as their shared history evolves. Existing benchmarks primarily supervise user facts and preferences or experience reusable across users, leaving this relationship-specific agent memory implicit. Additionally, most prior works measure the model solely with final-answer QA over long interaction histories, making the assessment still incomplete and unreliable. To this end, we introduce DyadMem with the proposed new definition User-conditioned Relational Agent Memory (URAM). DyadMem jointly annotates user-side memory and URAM along the same multi-session trajectories, resulting in 6 memory categories. To summarize, it includes 3,065 episodes, 50,961 sessions, and 61,210 QA instances, with extensive session-level Capture and Update gold annotations, query-level Recall support, and two QA settings: Gold-Memory and Full-Pipeline. Across 16 open-weight and 4 proprietary models, Gold-Memory QA is consistently strong, yet Full-Pipeline QA drops sharply. Such a gap explicitly supports our fine-grained evaluation design. Additionally, several quantitative results further reveal low Capture recall, incomplete Recall, and unsafe-deletion issues arising from even the frontier LLMs. We further conduct a rigorous experiment to validate the effectiveness of our URAM and observe the positive effects for all 20 models. In summary, DyadMem is a dual-domain, full-pipeline memory benchmark with extensive annotation efforts for advancing the domain's development.

items.title: ECOPOLITICS IN THE ANTHROPOCENE AND INTERSPECIES SOCIOTECHNICAL DESIGN
items.abstract: This article analyzes counterpoints among cosmopolitics, sympoiesis, ecosocialism, and "degrowth communism" in order to confront the crisis of the Anthropocene with new ways of doing sociotechnical/cosmopolitical design. It offers a critical-analytical literature review that confronts Bruno Latour's Actor-Network Theory, Donna Haraway's figurations, Nancy Fraser's ecosocialist formulations, Kohei Saito's degrowth communism, and Andrew Feenberg's Critical Theory of Technology. It investigates how overcoming modern dualisms and reductionisms enables a new understanding of technology as a field of economic and cosmopolitical dispute. It argues that the redemocratization of technical codes and multispecies justice require abandoning the logic of profit and unlimited growth in favor of an economy oriented toward use value and the sharing of wealth. The complementarity between ecological materialism and sociotechnical design reveals that confronting planetary depletion demands more than isolated engineering solutions; it presupposes a transenvironmental project, but also degrowth, technological democratization, and socio-environmental justice. The article concludes that the process of "staying with the trouble" in the Global South calls for a transformative praxis that integrates institutional re-design with mutual care and territorial solidarity, providing the foundation for a platform of convergence among ecopolitical struggles for the emancipatory co-production of existence.

items.title: EdgeAgent: Orchestrating On-Device LLM inference for End-User Multi-Agent Systems on CPU-GPU Unified Memory Architectures
items.abstract: Emerging multi-agent LLMs demand privacy-preserving edge deployment, yet current inference systems struggle with these collaborative workflows. Specifically, the memory-bound decode phase causes severe bus contention on unified memory architectures (UMA), paralyzing naive CPU-GPU co-execution. Furthermore, speculative decoding in multi-agent workloads faces extreme variance in drafting difficulty, alternating between complex reasoning and predictable structured generation. Compounded by frequent tool-induced stalls, this highly fragmented execution severely underutilizes hardware and defeats traditional static batching. We present EdgeAgent, a cross-layer inference system explicitly co-designed for edge UMA and multi-agent workloads. At the micro-architectural level, it bypasses rigid graph-compiler constraints to enable zero-copy UMA-aware tensor parallelism, utilizing asymmetric memory layouts to fully saturate both CPU and GPU compute units. At the scheduling level, it dynamically allocates draft budgets based on real-time sequence predictability to bound bandwidth waste. Concurrently, an asynchronous suspend-and-yield mechanism actively evicts stalled agents, ensuring continuous hardware saturation during unpredictable tool invocations. Extensive evaluations on an Apple M4 SoC demonstrate that the UMA-aware execution alone contributes a 1.29x speedup over batched speculative decoding. Adding the agent-aware scheduling lifts the full EdgeAgent system to a 1.77x speedup under extreme tool-use latencies.

items.abstract: Low Back Pain (LBP) is one of the musculoskeletal problems that may be associated with non-ergonomic working postures. Health center workers may perform their duties in sitting or standing positions for relatively long periods; therefore, adequate understanding of ergonomic practices and LBP prevention is needed. This Community Service (PkM) activity aimed to improve workers’ knowledge and awareness through ergonomic education and health promotion as an effort to prevent LBP at UPT Puskesmas Delitua, Deli Serdang Regency. The activity was conducted through educational sessions, discussions, demonstrations of ergonomic working postures, active breaks, and simple stretching exercises. A total of 65 health workers participated in the activity. Initial identification showed that 35 participants (53.8%) had ergonomic working postures, while 30 participants (46.2%) had non-ergonomic working postures. Based on the initial identification of complaints, 33 participants (50.8%) reported severe LBP symptoms, while 32 participants (49.2%) reported mild symptoms. These initial conditions served as the basis for developing and delivering educational materials covering proper working postures, adjustment of work facilities, implementation of active breaks, and regular stretching exercises. The activity provided participants with an opportunity to understand LBP risk factors and practice the application of more ergonomic working postures in their daily activities. This community service activity is expected to improve workers’ understanding, awareness, and practical skills in applying ergonomic principles as a promotive and preventive effort to reduce the risk of LBP in the workplace.

items.title: EEG-based mental workload recognition during multi-tasking scenarios: the role of resting-state normalization and brain region of EEG features
items.abstract: EEG-based mental workload (MWL) recognition is challenged by inter-individual variability and limited model interpretability. This study investigated MWL recognition in long-term multi-tasking scenarios using resting-state EEG normalisation and regional feature analysis. Participants performed multi-tasking operations at three difficulty levels, while resting-state and task-state EEG, behavioural performance, and NASA-TLX ratings were collected. The best whole-brain model achieved 93.78% ± 0.45% accuracy under standard normalisation, while the parietal configuration retained substantial recognition capability with fewer electrodes. Resting-state normalisation changed EEG feature-importance patterns, but its effects on classification were classifier-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial. SHAP analysis identified prominent frontal and parietal contributions. The findings support interpretable and lightweight EEG-based MWL monitoring in complex operational environments.

items.title: EFFECTIVENESS OF AN AI-BASED METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING ENGLISH ORAL COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE AMONG NON-LINGUISTIC UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
items.abstract: This article develops and theoretically substantiates an artificial-intelligence-based methodology for improving the English oral communicative competence of students in non-linguistic higher education institutions. The methodology rests on a Teacher–Learner–AI model in which artificial intelligence serves as a supplementary pedagogical resource rather than a replacement for teachers or authentic human communication. It comprises seven interconnected stages: diagnostic assessment, individualisation, AI-assisted preparation, AI-supported communication, feedback, human interaction, and reflection with reassessment. A quasi-experimental design is proposed for evaluating its effectiveness; the numerical values presented in the article are illustrative and are not offered as actual experimental findings. Oral communicative competence is treated as a five-component construct: linguistic accuracy, fluency, pronunciation and intelligibility, interactional competence, and pragmatic-strategic competence. The study argues that artificial intelligence increases opportunities for meaningful speaking practice only when its use is pedagogically structured and supervised by teachers.

items.title: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
items.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows humans to inspect how large language models reach their answers, and oversee model behaviour. This reasoning comes at an increased inference cost, motivating efficient methods that train models to solve tasks using fewer tokens. However, a common concern is that such training may cause models to skip important reasoning steps, so the CoT no longer faithfully reflects the model's decision. It is unclear whether or when this occurs in practice, since different efficiency methods apply length pressure to models' CoT in distinct ways, and faithfully explaining a model's decision takes more tokens on some tasks than others. To understand these dynamics, we fine-tune a variety of models with three methods that apply length pressure differently, namely a fixed generation budget, a per-example length target, and a group-relative length reward. We evaluate how efficient reasoning affects CoT faithfulness (i.e., how well the CoT reflects model decisions on related inputs) and monitorability (i.e., whether the CoT reveals when input interventions alter the output). We find that it affects faithfulness and monitorability differently. Faithfulness falls in most settings, primarily because the trained models are less consistent. Monitorability is more robust, as models keep acknowledging the influence on their answer even when the CoT is much shorter.

items.title: Emerging Applications of Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence in Schema Therapy: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Digital tools have become increasingly integrated into contemporary psychological practice, responding to the growing demand for accessible, scalable, and experiential mental health interventions. Within this evolving landscape, Schema Therapy represents a promising field for technological enhancement due to its emphasis on experiential techniques, mode work, and the restructuring of deeply rooted cognitive-emotional patterns. Objectives: This study aimed to map and characterize how Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence technologies are currently being used or proposed to support innovation in the application of Schema Therapy. Methods: A scoping review was conducted with searches performed across five major databases. Search strategies were adapted to each database, and records were screened according to inclusion/exclusion criteria. Results: Four records met eligibility criteria, revealing an emerging yet limited body of work dedicated to theoretical and experimental innovation in this area. Virtual Reality and metaverse-based interventions were proposed to create immersive, ecologically valid environments that facilitate emotional reprocessing, mode restructuring, and reductions in self-criticism, key mechanisms within ST. AI tools have demonstrated potential for large-scale identification of Early Maladaptive Schemas, enabling new forms of assessment and case conceptualization within online mental health contexts. Conclusions: No current evidence is sufficient to establish the efficacy of combining digital technologies such as Virtual Reality or Artificial Intelligence with Schema Therapy. The available literature remains limited and includes different stages of research development, from conceptual proposals and protocols to empirical studies. The identified applications primarily use these technologies as tools to support established Schema Therapy procedures rather than to modify its theoretical concepts or techniques. Although the findings indicate possible directions for technologically supported interventions, the current evidence is insufficient to establish their clinical effectiveness. Further empirical research is needed to evaluate their effects, feasibility, and clinical use within Schema Therapy.

items.title: Enhanced Visualization of Low Probability Trajectories
items.abstract: Forecast paths for hurricanes are commonly communicated through Cone of Uncertainty (COU) visualizations. An alternative visualization, animated risk trajectories (ARTs), uses dynamic ensembles of instances to convey an array of possible future tracks. Four experiments with simplified scenarios explored how surprising or misleading each form of visualization was for outcomes beyond the most likely forecast path, using participants with little direct experience (Colorado-based participants) versus more familiarity with hurricane risk and forecasts (Florida-based participants). For subsequent landfalls at locations farther from the central projected path, all participant types felt less misled when viewing ARTs rather than COUs. While Colorado-based participants reported less surprise when viewing discrepant outcomes following ARTs, Florida-based participants found deviant outcomes surprising regardless of the visualization used. Results suggest ARTs may help people better understand uncertainty when singular “most likely path” forecasts are wrong, although those expected to have greater experience may benefit less.

items.title: Enhancing Biomedical Named Entity Recognition via Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble Method
items.abstract: Instruction tuning has become a common paradigm for applying large language models (LLMs) to biomedical named entity recognition (BioNER). However, existing instruction-tuning approaches still face two key challenges. First, conventional natural-language instructions typically serialize BioNER annotations as flat textual outputs, providing limited structural constraints for typed entity extraction. Second, high-quality biomedical annotations are limited, and learning from a single serialized output form may restrict structural diversity and reduce model robustness. Although external biomedical knowledge can be introduced to alleviate data scarcity, it often requires costly resource construction. To address these challenges, we propose MITE, a Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble method for BioNER. MITE reformulates BioNER as a structure-to-structure generation task by representing both instructions and entity outputs in code-formatted representations. Specifically, each training instance is transformed into multiple programming-language formats, including Python, C++, and Java, while preserving the same underlying entity semantics. These language-specific representations provide structurally diverse supervision without requiring external biomedical knowledge or additional annotations. During inference, MITE aggregates predictions from different code formats through an entity-level voting strategy, reducing language-specific prediction variance and improving robustness. Experiments on six widely used BioNER datasets demonstrate that MITE consistently outperforms representative BERT-based and LLM-based baselines and exhibits strong cross-dataset generalization. Ablation and parameter analyses further verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed components.

items.title: Enhancing Digital Library Accessibility through Artificial Intelligence for Individuals with Disabilities: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Digital libraries are now the main route to scholarly content, yet their content, interfaces and services still exclude many disabled users, and promotion of artificial intelligence (AI) as a remedy has outpaced evidence that it works for them. Framed by the social model of disability and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), this systematic literature review, reported according to PRISMA 2020, examined which AI technologies have been applied to digital library accessibility, what has been measured, and what follows for disabled users. Boolean searches of OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, the Directory of Open-Access Journals, PubMed and ERIC identified 1,056 records; after removal of 429 duplicates and two-stage screening against explicit criteria (peer-reviewed, 2016–2025, English), 26 studies were included and synthesised thematically. Speech synthesis, speech recognition, natural language processing, document AI, optical character recognition, computer vision alt text and machine learning personalisation were studied, mostly for blind and print-disabled users. Coding every claim into three registers showed that 11 studies only describe what a technology does, 13 measure system or provider-side performance, and only two report outcomes measured with disabled users, both through self-report; this absence of outcome evidence is a principal finding. Audited conformance of scholarly documents is poor; disabled people appear mainly as beneficiaries, not co-designers. The review contributes an evidence-graded, five-stage integration model that specifies actors, gates and failure handling, and recommends treating AI outputs as unverified until evaluated with disabled users. Findings rest on single-reviewer screening and published records, and the model awaits empirical testing.

items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) expands across mental health services, questions arise about whether it can replace digital health navigators (DHNs), including those with lived experience. The DHN role generally resists automation because lived experience deepens specific dimensions that AI cannot replicate. Drawing on emerging evidence of AI's limitations in contextual reasoning, cultural sensitivity, and clinical safety, the authors identify where DHNs with lived experience are least substitutable: real-world knowledge of services, cultural grounding in the communities they serve, and relational trust. A practical model is also outlined in which AI augments DHN workflows through triage, documentation, and engagement monitoring.

items.title: Epistemological Friction in Artificial Intelligence Use among Humanities Faculty and Students in Western Mindanao, Philippines
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered higher education faster than institutional policy can regulate it, a gap visible in Philippine humanities programs, where interpretive originality and authorial voice are central to disciplinary practice. Humanities programs in regional, resource-constrained Philippine settings remain largely absent from the AI-adoption literature, a gap this study addressed by examining AI adoption, perceived usefulness and ease of use, perceived risk, AI literacy, and behavioral intention among humanities faculty and undergraduate students at a state university in Zamboanga City, Philippines, where no institutional AI policy exists. A convergent mixed-methods design combined survey data from 200 students and 23 faculty with ten in-depth interviews; quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Welch's t-test, while qualitative data underwent reflexive thematic analysis, integrated through joint display analysis. Students used AI moderately and selectively, favoring comprehension and organization over original composition. Faculty reported higher AI familiarity than students but markedly lower classroom use (M = 3.59 versus M = 2.67), a pattern proposed here as epistemological friction: principled disciplinary resistance rather than technical inability. Both groups perceived high risk, yet risk predicted only the intention to limit AI use (r = .531, p < .001), not the intention to discontinue it (r = .047, ns), producing concealed adoption tentatively labeled a shadow AI ecosystem. Perceived usefulness (β = .427) and ease of use (β = .365) were the strongest predictors of continued use, while students significantly outperformed faculty in AI literacy (d = -0.943), reversing the assumed top-down transmission of competence. AI acceptance here was shaped as much by disciplinary values and unclear institutional guidance as by usefulness or ease of use, supporting tiered governance, faculty development addressing disciplinary and ethical concerns, and structured reverse mentoring to narrow the literacy gap and reduce concealed AI use.

items.title: EpiWorld: Grounding LLM Policy Agents in Epidemiological World Models
items.abstract: Epidemic intervention policies are textual artefacts that human decision-makers interpret, justify, and revise through natural language, making large language models a natural candidate for epidemic policy reasoning. A naive LLM, however, lacks the epidemic dynamics needed to project intervention consequences, the quantitative surveillance signals required to assess severity, and the institutional constraints that define admissible actions. We present EpiWorld, a closed-loop framework that grounds an LLM policy actor in a learned action-conditioned epidemiological world model and a tiered skill library of public-health protocols, surveillance tools, and adaptive lessons accumulated through after-action analysis. Given a candidate intervention, the world model predicts regional epidemic evolution and enables fast counterfactual rollouts that provide feedback for policy selection and refinement. Outcomes of simulated futures are distilled into reusable lessons while protocol constraints remain fixed, allowing the decision process to improve without sacrificing interpretability or controllability. We evaluate both the world model and the end-to-end framework on retrospective COVID-19 and Influenza datasets: the world model achieves the best out-of-distribution Peak-MAE among all forecasting baselines, and the closed-loop framework reduces cumulative hospitalisation by up to 59% across datasets and by an average of ~16% across six LLM backbones, outperforming reinforcement-learning and optimal-control policy baselines.

items.title: Ergonomic Opportunistic Networks: A Human-Centric Architecture for Adaptive Resource Orchestration
items.abstract: Opportunistic networks acquire external communication, computation, sensing, storage, and service resources as mission requirements evolve. Prior research has developed human-mobility models, context-aware routing, trust mechanisms, and adaptive resource-management approaches, but these contributions address narrower decision scopes and do not by themselves provide an ergonomics-guided process for governing heterogeneous Helpers throughout mission execution. This paper formalises Ergonomic Opportunistic Networks (ErOppNets) as a technology-independent extension of mission-driven opportunistic networks in which ergonomics serves as a design compass for selecting and adapting technologies, policies, resources, and participation mechanisms to support human factors and ergonomics goals alongside mission performance. ErOppNets integrate human-centric, context-aware, trust-aware, and resource-aware decisions across discovery, assessment, admission, role allocation, monitoring, reassessment, reconfiguration, replacement, and release. A multidimensional orchestration model formalises Helper selection, while the ErOppNet Adaptive Orchestration (EAO) procedure translates the model into operational decisions. The evaluation compares six policies across nominal, dynamic, adversarial, resource scarcity, failure, and scalability scenarios using 100 paired random seeds per primary comparative configuration, complemented by separate parameter-sensitivity analyses. Under nominal conditions, EAO and Static Multidimensional (SM) selection achieved 100 per cent mission completion; relative to SM, EAO reduced mean configuration churn by 60.0 per cent. Across dynamic conditions and external populations up to 2000 entities, EAO preserved mission feasibility while balancing utility, stability, trust requirements, and adversarial exposure. The results support ErOppNets as a human-centric, adaptive, and technology-independent model for intelligent opportunistic network management.

items.title: Ethical Labour Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence and Automation
items.abstract: The fast adoption of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation is changing how organisations operate and govern labour. The conventional Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) models, which are predominantly directed toward philanthropy, cannot deal with emerging issues like the bias in algorithms, labor displacement, online surveillance, and risks of data governance. In this chapter, the author discusses the use of ethical labour governance in AI-driven workplaces and recommends a governance framework based on CSR, which incorporates responsible AI, algorithmic responsibility, and strategies aimed at inclusive workforce transition. The chapter provides insights into the conceptual analysis and case-driven knowledge to define governance mechanisms such as standards of transparency, reskilling programs, and multi-stakeholder control. In the study, the author has placed utmost importance on responsible automation as a means of balancing technological innovation and the dignity of workers, social equality, and long-term sustainability.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-as-a-Judge Beyond Score Alignment: A Psychometric Analysis of Residual Judging Difficulty
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used as automatic judges, with validity typically assessed via alignment with human scores. However, aggregate agreement fails to reveal whether humans and LLMs find the same evaluation cases difficult. In this paper, we study this problem in summarization evaluation from a psychometric perspective. We fit Many-Facet Rasch Models separately to human and LLM ratings to decompose scores into latent summary quality, rater severity, dimension severity, and rating-scale thresholds. Building on this decomposition, we define residual hardness as a model-adjusted measure of judging difficulty and compare whether human and LLM judges share the same hardness structure. Across 17 open-weight LLM judges on SummEval, we find that moderate alignment in latent summary quality does not imply alignment in residual hardness. Human and LLM judges differ in which summary--dimension units remain difficult, and this mismatch is strongly dimension-dependent. Consistency shows a pronounced LLM-hard shift, whereas coherence shows a human-hard shift. We further show that human-easy but LLM-hard cases are partially predictable from observable source--summary properties. These findings suggest that aggregate human alignment reflects only part of LLM-as-a-judge reliability, while psychometric residual diagnostics support more informative judge evaluation and more targeted human--LLM collaboration.

items.title: Evaluating VQA in Vision Language Models using Cooperative Principles
items.abstract: We evaluate the performance of Vision Language Models in Visual Question Answering (VQA) when questions violate Grice's maxims. To do this, we use VLMs to generate question modifiers that add non-essential, ambiguous or false information and show that in the presence of such violations, the VLMs that we evaluate (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Llava) show diminished performance. Further, we empirically show the difference between how humans reason pragmatically compared to VLMs, and the difference in VLM reasoning when it resolves violations that are human-induced compared to those that are AI-generated. Finally, we show that human cognitive effort (measured through time-on-task in an experiment) is lower for resolving VLM-induced violations, but VLMs themselves perform less accurately in such cases.

items.title: Evaluator-in-the-Loop Monte Carlo Tree Search via LLM Agents for Motif Scaffolding in Protein Design
items.abstract: Motif-scaffolding systems commonly follow a generate-then-filter paradigm, in which candidate proteins are generated independently and structural evaluation is used primarily for terminal screening or ranking. This paradigm underuses evaluation: failed predictions contain state-specific evidence about whether a design requires repair of motif geometry, global foldability, or other structural constraints. We introduce \textbf{ELMS} (Evidence-based LLM-guided Monte Carlo Search), an evaluator-in-the-loop search framework for motif scaffolding that turns such evaluator feedback into targeted design actions. Effective reuse of structural feedback is nontrivial because different scaffold states exhibit different failure modes, and repeatedly refining a single trajectory can prematurely commit computation to an unproductive region of sequence space. ELMS therefore retains evaluated scaffolds as persistent search states: a Critic Agent diagnoses state-local structural failures, a Policy Agent selects targeted operators with execution parameters, motif-locked operators realize legal sequence modifications, and MCTS determines which historical states should receive further design effort. Under the standard GeomMotif protocol (100 candidates per task), ELMS achieves Successful rates of 86.41\% on single-motif tasks and 84.57\% on paired-motif tasks, exceeding the strongest prior baseline by 19.3 and 21.9 percentage points, respectively. On MotifBench, under a matched 100-candidate search budget, it solves 26.7 of 30 tasks on average (88.89\% Task Success), compared with 16.0 tasks (53.33\%) for the strongest baseline. These results establish ELMS as an effective approach for converting structural evaluation from a terminal filter into actionable guidance for iterative motif scaffolding.

items.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for learning path recommendation (LPR) faces two coupled obstacles. First, the policy must commit to a sequence of L concepts without intermediate feedback, producing a combinatorial search space that grows super-exponentially with L and provides reward only at the final step. Second, expert learning paths would be the natural cure for sparse-reward RL, but they do not exist in educational data, because student logs record what learners did, not what they should have done. We address both obstacles by importing a recipe from simulator-based demonstration learning in robotics: the knowledge tracing simulator is used both to synthesize per-learner expert demonstrations through evolutionary search and to train a deployment-free policy that distills these demonstrations into a feed-forward learner. Our framework, EVOL, instantiates this pipeline with an asymmetric actor-critic where the actor commits to deployment-realistic blind planning while the critic exploits the privileged simulator state during training. Across three datasets (ASSIST15, Junyi, and EdNet; 39-189 concepts) and path lengths L = 5, 10, and 20, EVOL surpasses 8 baselines spanning heuristic, sequential, RL, graph-enhanced RL, and LLM-enhanced methods. We further compare three imitation strategies (BC, AWR, and DAPG) and show that final performance is governed by the quality of evolutionary experts rather than by the particular imitation objective.

items.title: Evolutionary Computation for Trustworthy AI: From Attacks and Defenses to Self-Evolving Era
items.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) has evolved from task-specific models to foundation models and agents, the scope of trustworthy AI has expanded from model-level robustness to the reliability and safety of broader AI systems. This evolution has also expanded the attack surface from individual models to broader system-level interactions, including tool use, context, and interaction trajectories with dynamic environments. As a result, maintaining reliable and safe behavior under changing or deliberately manipulated conditions has become increasingly challenging. The search for effective attacks and defenses often relies on black-box feedback to navigate discrete choices among words, actions, system components, or their combinations. Multiple objectives and expensive candidate evaluations further limit what can be explored. Evolutionary Computation (EC), with its population-based, gradient-free search and flexible variation and selection mechanisms, is well suited to these settings. This survey reviews how EC has been applied to trustworthy AI across three directions: evolutionary attacks, evolutionary defenses, and trustworthy self-evolving AI systems. Unlike prior reviews that treat trustworthy AI, EC, and self-evolving systems largely separately, we connect these lines through a common evolutionary perspective. For self-evolving AI, we examine how trustworthiness governs the generation and retention of updates that shape subsequent adaptation. We further synthesize evaluation methods and benchmark resources from both trustworthiness and evolutionary-search perspectives. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future research directions toward more effective and reliable use of EC in trustworthy AI.

items.title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark for Runtime Security Risks in Workspace Agents
items.abstract: Workspace agents combine large language models with execution harnesses to perform stateful, multi-step tasks that access or modify external resources. Existing benchmarks leave gaps in executable coverage of their runtime security risks, while evolving model capabilities, harnesses, tools, and threats motivate benchmark evolution. We introduce EvoRiskBench, an evolving benchmark organized around the EP-Path-EF framework, which links an initial risk entry point to a one-hop technical effect through an agent-mediated risk path. The framework defines nine entry-point categories and five effect categories; a 20-participant study supports their interpretability and classification consistency on representative cases. Guided by this framework, an automated end-to-end workflow constructs and executes risk cases in isolated environments and independently verifies outcomes using runtime traces and environment states. The benchmark provides a reproducible dataset of 450 adversarial tasks across six scenarios. We evaluate nine model-harness configurations spanning three models (GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, and Claude Opus 5) and three harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw). Our results reveal substantial vulnerabilities across systems. The most vulnerable configuration, Codex with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, reaches a 68.44% attack success rate (ASR), indicating that configuration of workspace agent is insufficient to ensure secure autonomous execution. ASR varies more across models than harnesses, and harness differences depend on the model. The benchmark cases and evaluation platform will be released after completion of artifact safety and reproducibility checks.

items.title: Examining the Impact of Learning Agility on Career Adaptability Through Workforce Agility in the Banking Sector
items.abstract: In this study, learning agility and its influence on career adaptability among banking employees was explored, in relation to workforce agility. The study employed a quantitative approach consisting of cross-sectional type which was conducted in the collection of the data in this study, the researcher used a structured questionnaire with respondents being 300 employees in the banking field. Openness to learning, learning from experience, feedback seeking, adaptability to new situations, and application of new knowledge were assessed as facets of learning agility. Workforce agility was measured as adaptability, proactivity, flexibility, responsiveness to change and resilience; and career adaptability was measured as career concern, control, curiosity and confidence. The proposed relationships were tested using descriptive and mediation analyses. The results indicated the learning agility (M = 3.82; SD = 0.64), workforce agility (M = 3.76; SD = 0.67) and career adaptability (M = 3.88; SD = 0.61) each had a mean score. The direct effects of learning agility on workforce agility were 0.62 and the effect of workforce agility on career adaptability was 0.44. The low direct effect of learning agility on career adaptability (e=0.27) was also observed. The indirect effect on the workforce agility was 0.34 with the 95% bootstrap confidence interval of 0.27-0.42, which failed to include zero. The results showed that the effect of Career Adaptability was fully mediated by Workforce Agility. items.title: Experimental Evaluation of Croton Megalocarpus Oil as a Bio-Based Cutting Fluid in Turning Inconel 718 Alloys
items.abstract: The use of conventional petroleum-based cutting fluids poses significant environmental and occupational health concerns, highlighting the need for biodegradable alternatives in modern manufacturing. Exposure to cutting-fluid mists and volatile compounds generated during machining can cause respiratory irritation, skin disorders, and asthma. This study investigated the performance of Croton megalocarpus oil as a bio-based cutting fluid for machining Inconel 718. The performance of three cutting fluids was compared: conventional mineral cutting oil, filtered Croton megalocarpus base oil, and Croton megalocarpus oil containing 0.5 wt% graphene nanoparticles. Turning experiments were conducted on a TSL-550D precision lathe under identical machining conditions for all three fluids. The results showed that pure Croton oil reduced the cutting temperature to 160 ℃, representing a 5.3% reduction compared with mineral oil (169 ℃). The graphene-enhanced Croton oil provided the greatest reduction in cutting temperature, with a mean value of 136 ℃, corresponding to a 19.5% reduction relative to mineral oil. It also produced the lowest surface roughness (1.68 μm), compared with 1.72 μm for pure Croton oil and 1.70 μm for mineral oil. These results indicate that graphene-enhanced Croton megalocarpus oil has potential as a bio-based alternative to conventional mineral cutting fluids for machining Inconel 718.

items.title: Explainable AI and Governance
items.abstract: To have an efficient artificial intelligence (AI) governance in the world that is characterised by increased auto-automation, it is vital to navigate the emergence of explainable AI (XAI). Since AI systems are used for making important decisions in fields as diverse as the financial industry or healthcare, their complexity (often due to the fact that they can be labelled as black boxes) becomes a critical burden when it comes to accountability, trust, and compliance with regulatory forces. This chapter discusses the role of XAI methods, which are supposed to make the reasoning of AI clear and comprehensible, as a key connection between technical AI-building and sound and ethical governance models. Explainability is not only an objective that is pursued at a technical level but also a socio-legal requirement. We explore the existing terrain, exploring and identifying various XAI solutions, including local and global explanations and model-agnostic and model-specific, and evaluating their potential usability by different interested parties, including regulators, system developers, and the impacted population. One of the main themes is the ability of explainability to be codified and go beyond the broad principles to provide quantifiable and enforceable benchmarks of algorithmic fairness and human control. Finally, to govern effectively, there needs to be explainability into the lifecycle of AI development in order to completely balance the element of power, preserve the trust of people, and be able to deliver an evenly distributed promise of AI in order to create a technology-friendly human-centred existence.

items.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence For Real-Time Cyber Attack Detection And Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Security operations centers rely on machine learning in increasing amounts when conducting network intrusion detection, but the inability to comprehend, trust, and act on alerts caused by black-box models is a significant issue under time pressure. Explainable AI (XAI) solutions such as SHAP and LIME provide solutions to the transparency problem, yet the explanation latency that they introduce makes them unsuitable for real-time triage of security alerts. This paper introduces an integrated XAI framework that consists of a Random Forest-XGBoost soft voting model along with a latency-aware dual mode explanation engine that uses the optimal LIME path for real-time query explanation and the approximated KernelSHAP path for forensic query explanation. A feature weighted risk scoring component transforms explanation attribution scores into a risk score bound in real time. Using the UNSW-NB15 dataset, we show that the framework provides state-of-the-art detection performance comparable to black box baselines with explanation latency well within real-time bounds and high attribution stability for forensic purposes.

items.title: Exploring ChatGPT as a Consumer Decision Tool for Restaurant Selection in Indonesia
items.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence in consumer decision-making has changed the way consumers search for, evaluate, and purchase hospitality services. In Jakarta, where dining options are diverse and highly competitive, this study examines how trust and social influence shape consumers' decisions to use ChatGPT for restaurant recommendations. Data were collected from 322 respondents who had used ChatGPT for restaurant selection and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. Trust has a positive and substantial effect on decision-making, indicating that users are more willing to follow ChatGPT's suggestions when they believe it is credible, dependable, and useful. Social influence also has a positive effect, indicating that peer encouragement, social approval, and the normalization of AI use increase reliance on ChatGPT. Together the two constructs explain 67.5 percent of the variance in decision-making, offering insight for restaurant operators, AI developers, and digital marketers in emerging markets.

items.title: Exploring Dragging Interaction on Curved Displays in Virtual Reality
items.abstract: As virtual reality (VR) environments increasingly incorporate curved displays, dragging interactions on such displays have become more common. However, evidence on how display geometry affects dragging remains limited. We examined dragging performance and subjective workload using controller-based ray casting in two repeated-measures experiments with 12 participants each. Experiment 1 used curvilinear measurements, whereas Experiment 2 used angular measurements. Both manipulated display curvature, viewing depth, target amplitude and width. The results show that, compared with flat displays, curved displays with specific curvature settings yielded shorter movement times, lower error rates, and lower subjective workload. Increasing depth reduced movement time under curvilinear measurement but increased it under angular measurement. We further evaluated existing Fitts’ law adaptations and proposed an extension of the two-part model that incorporates display curvature. These findings inform the design and modeling of dragging interactions on curved VR displays.

items.title: Exploring Human–AI Collaboration and Strategic Decision-Making in UAE Government Institutions: Reconfiguring Leadership and Human Judgement in the
items.abstract: This study investigates human–AI collaboration and strategic decision-making in UAE government institutions, examining how artificial intelligence is transforming leadership practices, decision processes and human judgement. Although AI is integral to the UAE’s digital government transformation, existing research has focused mainly on technological adoption, organisational performance and digital transformation, leaving limited understanding of how human–AI collaboration reconfigures strategic decision-making and leadership responsibilities. The study addresses this gap by examining the relationship between human judgement and AI-enabled decision support, the effects of collaboration on strategic decision-making and organisational transformation, and emerging leadership challenges in AI-enabled governance. An exploratory qualitative research design was employed, drawing on academic literature, policy documents, official government publications and other documentary sources. The data were analysed thematically, guided by Dynamic Capabilities Theory, to identify patterns related to collaboration, decision-making, leadership transformation and human judgement. Findings show that AI is moving strategic decision-making towards collaborative arrangements in which AI provides analytical capabilities, predictive insights and decision support, while human leaders retain responsibility for contextual interpretation, ethical reasoning and final judgement. The study contributes by extending understanding of AI-enabled leadership through a human–AI collaboration perspective, demonstrating how technological capabilities and human judgement can be integrated within government decision processes. It concludes that effective AI governance requires complementarity rather than leadership displacement. Future research should examine these dynamics through empirical studies involving government leaders and employees across different UAE institutions and comparative public-sector contexts and broader institutional outcomes. The study recommends strengthening AI literacy, leadership capabilities, institutional readiness and responsible governance.

items.title: Exploring suicide among immigrant farmworkers in the United States: evidence from the National Violent Death Reporting System
items.abstract: Background Agricultural workers face some of the highest suicide rates in the United States, yet limited research has examined suicide among immigrant and migrant farmworkers (IMFs), a population recognized as particularly vulnerable within occupational health surveillance priorities. This study examined circumstances contributing to suicide among IMFs and compared these to circumstances among U.S.-born farmworkers using National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) data. Methods This multiple methods study used NVDRS data from 2013 to 2023, restricted to decedents in agricultural worker occupations (SOC Minor Group 45–2000) who died by suicide. Decedents were classified as IMFs (foreign-born) or U.S.-born based on birthplace. Bivariate analyses examined associations between nativity and reported circumstances preceding suicide, followed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, race, ethnicity, marital status, and education. A single-author qualitative analysis of investigative narratives, using an iterative inductive coding process with peer debriefing as a rigor check, identified themes describing IMF suicide circumstances. Results Of 1,162 decedents, 17% ( n = 201) were foreign-born. IMFs were older, more likely male, more likely Hispanic, and had lower educational attainment than U.S.-born decedents. IMFs were less likely to die by firearm (22% vs. 57%) and more likely to die by hanging/strangulation/suffocation (64% vs. 30%). In adjusted analysis, Hispanic ethnicity (OR = 0.014), older age (OR = 0.961), and being married (OR = 0.366) were associated with lower odds, while firearm method (OR = 2.126) was associated with higher odds, of U.S.-born status. Investigative documentation completeness did not differ significantly by nativity. Qualitative analysis identified four themes: stigma and avoidance of mental health care; violent and conflictual intimate relationships; substance use and associated familial shame; and immigration-related vulnerability and compounded isolation. Conclusion IMFs experience intersectional stressors—including immigration-related vulnerability, stigma, and isolation—that shape suicide risk in ways distinct from U.S.-born farmworkers, and that align with constructs of thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness from the Interpersonal-Psychological Theory of Suicide. Predominant use of hanging/strangulation among IMFs highlights limitations of conventional lethal means restriction strategies for this population. Culturally responsive, community-based, and workplace interventions—including stigma reduction, social connection programming, and multilingual lethal means safety messaging—are needed to address suicide risk among this underrecognized and vulnerable occupational group.

items.title: Family-Supported Personal Hygiene Education for Improving Dermatitis-Related Knowledge Among Agricultural Workers: A Case Study
items.abstract: Dermatitis is a common occupational health concern among agricultural workers, who are frequently exposed to environmental irritants, pesticides, fertilizers, plants, and prolonged sunlight exposure. Inadequate knowledge and suboptimal personal hygiene practices may further increase the risk of persistent skin problems. This study aimed to describe the application of personal hygiene health education, combined with family-supported mentoring, to address a knowledge deficit in a farmer with dermatitis. A case study design was conducted in the working area of the Padang Community Health Center involving a 53-year-old sugarcane farm laborer and her family. The intervention was implemented over seven consecutive days. It consisted of four visits, two structured educational sessions focused on recognizing dermatitis and appropriate personal hygiene practices, and continuous family-supported mentoring. Knowledge was assessed using pre-intervention and post-intervention questionnaires, while relevant behavioral responses were documented throughout the intervention period. The participant demonstrated several misconceptions about dermatitis and suboptimal hygiene practices at baseline, including delayed bathing, inconsistent handwashing, and reusing field clothing. Following the intervention, the knowledge score increased from 72.5 to 90, indicating improved understanding of dermatitis and recommended personal hygiene practices. Family-supported educational mentoring was associated with improved knowledge and may represent a feasible nursing approach to strengthening self-management of dermatitis among agricultural workers. Larger studies using validated instruments, comparative designs, and longer follow-up periods are required to evaluate the effectiveness and sustainability of this intervention.

items.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment
items.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models have scaled rapidly to enhance manipulation performance and generalizability, but this scaling incurs high computational costs that render real-world deployment increasingly challenging. Existing approaches typically mitigate this issue by designing smaller architectures or reducing the iterative denoising steps in flow-based policies. In this work, we propose FastOPD, a foundation-to-lightweight VLA framework that enables the practical deployment of large-scale VLAs through efficient on-policy distillation. Specifically, FastOPD adapts a flow map for single-state teacher supervision and combines it with a self-consistency objective to construct a compact student that learns the teacher dynamics. Furthermore, we theoretically demonstrate that minimizing this objective allows the distilled student to recover a distribution on par with that induced by an ideal few-step teacher model. We evaluate FastOPD across diverse foundation policies in simulation and real-world experiments. On LIBERO, FastOPD retains 84% of the performance of $π_{0.5}$ with only two inference steps, reducing inference latency by 78.1% while outperforming existing few-step distillation baselines in average success rate. With LingBot-VLA as the teacher, FastOPD improves the single-step success rate over the base student by 15.9 percentage points on RoboTwin 2.0. We further demonstrate its applicability to a World Action Model (WAM) and deploy a compact student distilled from MolmoAct2 on a real robot.
